questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best detective novels ever written in English
How to read faster and remember more of a book
How reading in groups can help people feel better
Why so many local libraries are closing down
questions.why: They discuss 'bibliotherapy' and how books can help us relax and feel more alive.

questions.q: Why does Georgina enjoy crime fiction?
options: She gets involved in working out who the killer is
It helps her fall asleep quickly at night
It is very relaxing after a long, busy day
It teaches her a lot about real crimes in history
questions.why: She says it's not exactly relaxing, but she gets involved trying to work out who the murderer is.

questions.q: What did the charity Reading Agency do in 2013?
options: It opened lots of new libraries around the country
It gave free books to children in poor areas
It started online reading groups for older people
It published a list of books doctors could offer
questions.why: Neil says it published a list of books that doctors could offer to patients.

questions.q: How successful has the scheme been?
options: It has only been used by doctors
1.2 million readers have borrowed its books
It has closed because of low interest
It is only for children
questions.why: Georgina says 1.2 million readers have borrowed the scheme's books and it will be extended to children.

questions.q: According to Philip Davis, what happens when people just scan a text?
options: Their brain gets very excited
They remember more information
It is fast, easy and automatic
They feel more emotional
questions.why: He says if you're just scanning for information, 'you go fast, it's very easy, it's automatic'.

questions.q: What happens in the brain when people read literature they care about, according to Davis?
options: Different parts become active and it comes to life
The brain slows down and has a chance to rest
Only the left side of the brain starts working
The reader slowly loses concentration and focus
questions.why: He says the brain works from a different hemisphere, gets excited and 'you can see the brain coming to life'.

questions.q: How can the benefits of group reading be measured?
options: By asking readers to take a written test afterwards
By counting how many books they read each month
By checking their heart rate before and after
By recording brain activity with electrodes or scans
questions.why: Davis mentions electrodes on the scalp measuring electricity, or an FMRI scanner showing blood flow.

questions.q: Why does Georgina joke about a detective story being 'really stimulating'?
options: Detective stories are used in all reading groups
It links the idea of a stimulus to her love of crime
She wants Neil to recommend a good one to read
Scientists have proved that detective stories are best
questions.why: After Neil says a poem or novel could be a stimulus, she jokes about her favourite genre, detective stories.
